data.summary: Added a `STALE` problem code (declared last) with a `Problem.stale(inputIndex, requestId, ageInDays)` factory, and taught `WorkRequestValidator` an optional clock/threshold constructor that rejects requests whose age strictly exceeds `maxAgeDays`, keeping the no-arg constructor behaviour unchanged and running the check only on otherwise-valid requests. Wired it through a new `Clock` bean and a `StalenessProperties` record (`app.staleness`, `@DefaultValue("30")`) in `ProcessingConfig`; `BatchObserver` needed no change because it already registers one counter per `ProblemCode` value.
uncertainties: I could not see src/main/resources/application.yml, so I did not touch it; the 30-day default comes from @DefaultValue("30"). If a test asserts the yml literally contains app.staleness.max-age-days: 30, that key still needs adding under the existing app: block.

The validator's own IllegalArgumentException message for maxAgeDays < 1 is "maxAgeDays must be at least 1, was <value>"; the property-prefixed message specified in the criteria lives in StalenessProperties.
Stale age is reported as whole days via Duration.toDays() (truncating), which matches the pinned 58-day example but means e.g. 30 days + 1 second reads as "30 days old".
